dossier.public_summary: The dip is not on the target star: image-centroiding puts it about 46 arcseconds away at high significance. Its depth also changes by more than a factor of two between sectors from the same instrument. Together this is best explained by an eclipsing binary on a nearby star blended in the TESS aperture, not a planet transiting the target.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip 45.9" from the target at 9.5 sigma, strong evidence the eclipse is not on the target but on a nearby star blending into the aperture. No suspect is <3 sigma from the centroid, consistent with centroid being driven by one sector but still off-target.

Depth changes significantly between sectors even within the same TESS-SPOC product (changes_within_a_source). Alone this can happen for diluted sources, but with an off-target centroid it supports a blend where aperture contamination varies by sector, not a planet on the target.
